title: DARPA Grand Challenges → Google self-driving car project / Waymo
summary: DARPA ran prize competitions for autonomous vehicles: the 2004 Grand Challenge (no finisher), the 2005 Grand Challenge (won by Stanford's 'Stanley') and the 2007 Urban Challenge (won by Carnegie Mellon's 'Boss'). The competitions ended; DARPA did not own or hand over the teams' vehicles or code as a program asset. Google started a self-driving car project in 2009, led by Sebastian Thrun and staffed by challenge veterans including Chris Urmson, Mike Montemerlo and Anthony Levandowski; it became Waymo, an Alphabet company, in 2016. The tie is people moving from university challenge teams to Google, not a transfer, license or contract.

links.claim: The last DARPA challenge, the Urban Challenge, was held Nov 3, 2007; Google's self-driving car project began in 2009, roughly two years later.

claims.claim: Waymo is DARPA's self-driving car program handed to Google.
claims.explanation: The people link is real and well documented: Google's project was led by the head of Stanford's 2005-winning team and staffed by veterans of the Stanford, Carnegie Mellon and Berkeley challenge entries. But DARPA ran time-limited prize competitions, not a vehicle program it later closed and transferred; DARPA's own timeline describes prizes awarded to university teams, and no license, asset transfer or contract from DARPA to Google is documented. Google hired the people rather than receiving the program.
